'''Spencer Janney Bloch''' (born May 22, 1944)<ref>[http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~bloch/cv Spencer Bloch CV], Department of Mathematics, [[University of Chicago]]. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref> is an American mathematician known for his contributions to [[algebraic geometry]] and [[algebraic K-theory|algebraic ''K''-theory]]. Bloch is the R. M. Hutchins Distinguished Service Professor Emeritus in the Department of Mathematics of the [[University of Chicago]].

==Research==
Bloch introduced the [[Bloch group]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite book | last= Bloch | first= S. | contribution= Applications of the dilogarithm function in algebraic K-theory and algebraic geometry | title= Proc. Int. Symp. on Alg. Geometry | editor-last= Nagata | editor-first= M | location= Tokyo | publisher= Kinokuniya | year= 1978 | pages= 103–114 }}</ref> He introduced [[Bloch's higher Chow group]], a generalization of [[Chow group]]s, in 1986.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bloch | first1=Spencer | title=Algebraic cycles and higher K-theory | journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] | volume=61 | date=September 1986 | issue=3 | pages=267–304 | doi=10.1016/0001-8708(86)90081-2 | doi-access=free}}</ref> He also introduced [[Bloch's formula]] in [[Algebraic K-theory]].<ref>[[Daniel Quillen]]: Higher algebraic K-theory: I. In: H. Bass (ed.): Higher K-Theories. Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol. 341. Springer-Verlag, Berlin 1973. {{ISBN|3-540-06434-6}}</ref>

Bloch and [[Kazuya Kato]] formulated the [[Norm residue isomorphism theorem|motivic Bloch–Kato conjecture]] relating [[Milnor K-theory]] and [[Galois cohomology]] in 1986<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bloch|first1=Spencer|last2=Kato|first2=Kazuya|title=p-adic etale cohomology|journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|date=1986|volume=63|pages=107–152|doi=10.1007/bf02831624}}</ref> and the [[Special values of L-functions#Conjectures|Bloch–Kato conjectures for special values]] of [[L-function|''L''-function]]s in 1990.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Kings | first1=Guido | title=The Bloch–Kato conjecture on special values of ''L''-functions. A survey of known results | url=http://jtnb.cedram.org/item?id=JTNB_2003__15_1_179_0 |mr=2019010 | year=2003 | journal=Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux | issn=1246-7405 | volume=15 | issue=1 | pages=179–198 | doi= 10.5802/jtnb.396| doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Bloch is a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110604020526/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/522935353?pg=vprof&mbr=1001811&returl=http:%2F%2Fwww.nasonline.org%2Fsite%2FDir%2F522935353%3Fpg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link Bloch, Spencer J.] [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]. Accessed January 12, 2010. Election Citation: "Bloch has done pioneering work in the application of higher algebraic K-theory to algebraic geometry, particularly in problems related to algebraic cycles, and is regarded as the world's leader in this field. His work has firmly established higher K-theory as a fundamental tool in algebraic geometry."</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>[http://www.amacad.org/enewsletter/a.pdf  American Academy of Arts & Sciences, NEWLY ELECTED MEMBERS, APRIL 2009] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130808142723/http://www.amacad.org/enewsletter/a.pdf |date=August 8, 2013 }}, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref><ref name="chr">[http://chronicle.uchicago.edu/090430/aaas.shtml Scholars, visiting faculty, leaders represent Chicago as AAAS fellows], The University of Chicago Chronicle, April 30, 2009, Vol. 28 No. 15. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref> and of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved November 10, 2012.</ref>

He received a [[Humboldt Prize]] in 1996.<ref>[https://www.uchicago.edu/about/documents/provost/provost_report19951996.shtml Annual Report of the Provost, 1995–96], [[University of Chicago]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref> He also received a 2021 [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6469 American Mathematical Society Announcement, November 19, 2020]. Accessed November 25, 2020.</ref>

At the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], he gave an invited lecture in 1978<ref>{{cite book|author=Bloch, S.|chapter=Algebraic K-theory and zeta functions of elliptic curves|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (Helsinki, 1978)|pages=511–515|year=1978}}</ref> and a plenary lecture in 1990.<ref name="chr"/><ref>{{cite book|author=Bloch, S.|chapter=Algebraic K-theory, motives, and algebraic cycles|pages=43–54|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, August 21–29, 1990, Kyoto, Japan|year=1991|publisher=Mathematical Society of Japan}}</ref> He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in  1981–82.<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/ Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref>
